THOUGHT: This 71-year-old male presents with systemic “B symptoms” — fatigue, malaise, and significant unintentional weight loss (18.1 kg over 6 months, ~40 lbs), which is highly concerning for an underlying malignancy or chronic inflammatory/infectious process. His history of prior non-seminomatous testicular cancer raises concern for secondary malignancy or late recurrence, but the current physical findings — bilateral cervical and inguinal lymphadenopathy plus splenomegaly — strongly suggest a hematolymphoid disorder. The CBC shows lymphocytosis, and flow cytometry confirms monoclonal B lymphocytes with a phenotype consistent with chronic lymphocytic leukemia/small lymphocytic lymphoma (CLL/SLL). CLL/SLL is the most common adult leukemia in Western countries, typically presenting in older adults with asymptomatic lymphocytosis, but advanced or symptomatic disease can manifest with B symptoms, lymphadenopathy, organomegaly (e.g., splenomegaly), and cytopenias. His normal-to-slightly-decreased hemoglobin and normal-to-decreased platelets are consistent with early bone marrow infiltration or immune-mediated cytopenias sometimes seen in CLL. While other conditions (e.g., lymphoma, autoimmune disease, occult infection, or metastatic solid tumor) must be considered in the differential for weight loss and lymphadenopathy, the flow cytometry result is diagnostic — it identifies a clonal B-cell population with the characteristic immunophenotype (CD5+, CD23+, CD43+, weak surface immunoglobulin, dim CD20/CD79b) that defines CLL/SLL. No further testing is needed to establish the diagnosis; however, staging (e.g., CT imaging, bone marrow biopsy, FISH, IGHV mutation status, TP53 sequencing) is indicated to guide prognosis and treatment decisions.

DIAGNOSIS: Chronic lymphocytic leukemia/small lymphocytic lymphoma (CLL/SLL)
